clues: This planned city sits far inland, well west of the sea coast. A range of hills stands to its south and west, the start of high ranges.
Frost bites here on winter mornings, yet snow hardly ever settles in the city centre. The high hills nearby catch snow while the valleys stay in rain shadow.
When the colonies joined as one nation in 1901, they needed a seat of their own. This city was founded and given its name in 1913 for that job.
Sydney and Melbourne both hoped to be the capital. Chiefs picked this fresh spot as a deal, so that neither city won.
Parliament meets in this city to make the laws of Australia. Its top court and the main offices of state stand here too.
